keyframe_review.note: 55,447 km2 (238 cells; Cliopatria's bbox 16.7-21.0 E, 50.7-54.9 N): Kuyavia (Inowrocław, Bydgoszcz, Brześć), Sieradz, Łęczyca, Łódź, Wieluń and Gdańsk Pomerania, the Piast land that no other Cliopatria row covers in 1279-1304 (the rows for Łęczyca, Kuyavia and Kalisz end by 1219). No page opened defines it as a state or gives its area. The Fragmentation page: Pomerelia 'became independent of the Polish dukes from 1227', so Gdańsk Pomerania (54 of the shape's 238 cells lie in the gazetteer's Pomerelia) is taken out for 1279-1293.

Same shape as 1279. The Fragmentation page has Przemysł II of Greater Poland hold 'Gdańsk Pomerania from 1294' and be assassinated soon after his coronation of 1295; the Greater Poland dossier reads his rule of Pomerelia as 1294-1296. Gdańsk Pomerania is therefore not Duchies-of-Poland land for 1294-1295.

correction.text: Cliopatria's whole shape including Gdańsk Pomerania

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Cliopatria shape with Gdańsk Pomerania again, 1296-1304. The pages opened do not say who held Pomerelia after Przemysł II's death (the Greater Poland dossier records its loss to this row in 1296); the Fragmentation page has Wenceslaus II of Bohemia 'King of Poland in 1300'.

region.text: the Cliopatria shape without Gdańsk Pomerania

ledger.note: 1279: Cliopatria begins to draw the Piast duchies of Kuyavia, Sieradz and Łęczyca as one entity. No page opened gives a founding: the Testament page describes the division of 1138 ('a period of nearly 200 years of Poland's feudal fragmentation' on the Fragmentation page), in which Łęczyca and Sieradz were held by Salomea of Berg for life and western Kuyavia went to the Seniorate Province; the year 1279 is Cliopatria's.

1296: Gdańsk Pomerania passes to this entity in Cliopatria. The Fragmentation page has Przemysł II hold it 'from 1294' and be assassinated soon after his crowning of 1295; it does not say who took the land. The Greater Poland dossier carries the matching loss.

1304: the last year of Cliopatria's Duchies of Poland shape. The Fragmentation page: Wenceslaus II 'became King of Poland in 1300'; from 1304 Władysław I challenged Wenceslaus II and III and, after 1306, 'took lands north through Kuyavia to Gdańsk Pomerania'. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape covers 237 of the 238 cells from 1305.

wars.name: Reunification of Poland under Władysław I the Elbow-high
wars.outcome: Władysław challenged Wenceslaus II and III from 1304; after Wenceslaus III's murder in 1306 he took Lesser Poland and 'lands north through Kuyavia to Gdańsk Pomerania', conquered Greater Poland in 1313-1314 and was crowned at Kraków in 1320.
wars.note: Brandenburg conquered Pomerania in 1308 and the Teutonic Knights then took Gdańsk Pomerania and kept it (same page).

certainty.note: A Cliopatria composite of Piast duchies; the pages opened give no borders for it.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Duchies of Poland' (1279-1293 and 1294-1304, two identical shapes of 55,447 km2) is not a state any page defines: it is the Piast land left over when the named duchies (Greater Poland, Masovia, Sandomierz, Silesia, Opole, Kraków) are drawn, i.e. Kuyavia, Sieradz, Łęczyca, Wieluń and Gdańsk Pomerania. The Testament page (the Wikipedia title Cliopatria gives) is about the 1138 division and mentions none of the years 1279-1304; the Fragmentation page adds only Pomerelia (independent from 1227), Przemysł II (Gdańsk Pomerania from 1294, crowned 1295), Wenceslaus II (King in 1300) and Władysław (1304-1320). A better dossier would split the shape into the Duchy of Kuyavia, the Duchy of Sieradz-Łęczyca and Pomerelia (Mestwin II of Pomerelia, unnamed on the pages opened): the additions batch eu-15-x is to cover the Polish duchies, and a gap-filler should open the pages of Kuyavia, Sieradz and Łęczyca. The page 'Testament of Bolesław III Wrymouth' dates the testament to about January 1115, not 1138. The Cliopatria Kingdom of Poland shape of 1305-1310 holds Gdańsk although the Fragmentation page has the Teutonic Order take it in 1308: for the Kingdom of Poland and Teutonic Order dossiers. No capital is recorded: the entity has no seat. Gazetteer lacks Sieradz, Łęczyca, Wieluń and Dobrzyń.
